concept_summary: La Gallinita is a restaurant with full cooking serving beer and wine (ABC Type 41) at 2989 24th St in San Francisco's NCT-24th-Mission district, inside the Mission Alcoholic Beverage and Calle 24 Special Use Districts.

overall.line: Of the 4 approvals this concept needs: 1 further review (zoning and use), 2 insufficient information (alcohol licence, building permit and change of use), 1 allowed (health permit).

lines.text: The concept is looked up as a Restaurant (Planning Code § 102).
Zoning district NCT-24TH-MISSION: a Restaurant on the first story is a conditional use (Planning Code § 763, in force from 2024-01-14 (Ord. 249-23, File No. 230701)).
No story is stated, so the first story was read.

Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District: Any proposed Restaurant in the sub-area east of the western boundary of the Mission Street NCT and north of Cesar Chavez Street needs Conditional Use, with or without alcohol. Zoning district NCT-24TH-MISSION lies inside that sub-area: a conditional use (Planning Code § 249.60(f)(1), in force since before 2022-01-01).

Calle 24 Special Use District: A new Restaurant, Limited Restaurant or Bar, or the physical expansion of an existing one, is prohibited where those uses take up, or would take up with the project, more than 35% of the commercial frontage (in linear feet) within 300 feet of the site inside the district. The records do not show that share of frontage, so this is not decided (Planning Code § 249.59(d)(1), in force since before 2022-01-01).

Calle 24 Special Use District: Section 249.59 itself does not make a Restaurant, Limited Restaurant or Bar a Conditional Use; its only Conditional Use triggers are storefront mergers over 799 square feet, replacing a Legacy Business and a first-story Health Service. Whether the use needs Conditional Use comes from the underlying district table. This rule asks for nothing here (Planning Code § 249.59(d)(2), in force since before 2022-01-01).

Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District: A Restaurant operating as a Bona Fide Eating Place may serve alcohol; its licence may be transferred from inside or from outside the district. The district adds no Conditional Use for the licence itself (but see subsection (f)(1) for the Restaurant use in the sub-area). This rule asks for nothing here (Planning Code § 249.60(b)(1)(A), in force since before 2022-01-01).

Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District: The § 202.2 operating conditions apply to every liquor establishment in the district; new, relocated or expanded ones, and any with a licence referred to Planning by ABC, must also provide outside lighting, keep window signage to 33% and keep 50% clear glazing on street-facing facades. This is a requirement, not a control (Planning Code § 249.60(d), in force since before 2022-01-01).

Hours: the description gives no closing time. Hours that are not principally permitted begin at 2 a.m. or later here (P 06:00-02:00; C 02:00-06:00; Planning Code § 763, in force since before 2022-01-01); the rules did not check a closing time after 2 a.m.

The records do not show what the space is used as, and the description does not say what it was last used as, so whether the proposed use (Restaurant) is a change of use is not established.

findings.text: Calle 24 Special Use District prohibits a new restaurant where restaurants, limited restaurants and bars take up, or would with the project take up, more than 35% of commercial frontage (linear feet) within 300 feet of the site; the records do not show that share of frontage per Planning Code § 249.59(d)(1).
findings.verification_note: The record does not contain the 35% commercial frontage rule, 300-foot measurement, or subsection (d)(1) cited in the sentence.

findings.text: Nine restaurant conditional use authorizations on the 24th Street corridor between Alabama and Mission (within 130 meters) were approved over the last 35 years, including 2956 24th St (57 m, 2019), 2962 24th St (51 m, 2011), 2980 24th St (43 m, 2001 and 1990), 2965 24th St (41 m, 1997) and 2969–2973 24th St (28 m, 2003); no restaurant CUA in this area was denied.
findings.verification_note: The cited records show only six restaurant CUAs, not nine, and do not establish that no CUAs were denied in the area.

findings.text: The directly adjacent property at 2990 24th St (43 m) has held continuous restaurant approvals since 1990 and operates with an active Type 41 ABC license as of 2022, demonstrating Commission acceptance of restaurant use next door.
findings.verification_note: The planning approvals are for 2980 24th St, not 2990 24th St; the records do not state the conclusion about Commission acceptance.

findings.text: The Commission imposed hours limited to 6 AM–2 AM daily, standard eating-and-drinking conditions (sidewalk maintenance within one block, soundproofing, odor control, waste management) and appointment of a community liaison officer at 2956 24th St in 2019.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Extension of CUA for change from limited restaurant to restaurant at 2937 24th St, 79 meters away, same zoning and SUD, decided February 2025 (6-0 vote). This is the most recent use decision on the immediate 24th Street corridor and shows the Commission continues to approve restaurant use conversions with standard conditions.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Approved 6-0 with conditions incorporating the prior Motion 19520; the extension request (filed December 2024, decided February 2025) took 10 weeks and confirms restaurant uses remain approved in this district when operators maintain compliance with standard conditions. The original 2015 CUA converted La Victoria Bakery to allow alcohol service as a bona fide eating place.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Change of use to full-service restaurant (Pig and Pie) at 2962 24th St, 51 meters away, within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Restricted Use Sub-District, filed May 2011 and approved September 2011. This is a use decision showing Commission approval for a retail-to-restaurant conversion in the same SUD.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Approved outright (no extracted conditions beyond standard) after 4 months for a full-service restaurant in the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD. The record notes it is not a formula retail use, confirming the Commission approved an independent restaurant on this block in the SUD without unusual restrictions.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: New full-service restaurant at 2900–2904 24th St, 130 meters west along the same corridor, same NCT-24th-Mission zoning, filed May 2011 and approved September 2011. This is a use decision for a new restaurant establishment (not a change of ownership).
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Approved outright in 4 months with no extracted special conditions. Shows the Commission routinely approved new full-service restaurants on the 24th Street corridor in 2011 when the application was complete and the use met district requirements.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Full-service restaurant approval at 2980 24th St, 43 meters away (directly adjacent property), same zoning, filed December 2000 and approved April 2001. This is a use decision at the neighboring address showing the site's immediate context has supported restaurant use for over two decades.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Approved after 4.5 months for a full-service restaurant under Planning Code Section 727.42. The adjacent property at 2990 24th St now holds an active Type 41 ABC license (on-sale beer and wine, eating place) as of 2022, demonstrating sustained Commission and ABC approval for restaurant alcohol service at the address next door.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: ABC Type 41 referral approval for continuation of existing restaurant (Tacos del Barrio) at 2817 24th St, 271 meters west, same NCT-24th-Mission zoning, decided March 2023. This is an agency referral (Planning answering ABC) but it confirms Planning's current position that Type 41 licenses are permitted in this district when operated as bona fide eating places.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning recommended approval of the Type 41 license, noting the restaurant must operate as a bona fide eating place and is subject to conditions under Planning Code Section 202.2(a). This referral shows Planning consistently supports beer-and-wine service in restaurants on the 24th Street corridor as of 2023.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Conditional use for a small self-service restaurant at 2969–2973 24th St, 28 meters away (almost directly across the street), same zoning, filed January 2003 and approved March 2003. This is a use decision showing the Commission approved restaurant use at the address immediately opposite La Gallinita's site.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Approved in under 2 months for a self-service restaurant, demonstrating the Commission's long-standing support for restaurant uses on this specific block of 24th Street even before the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD was formalized.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Conversion of retail store to small self-service restaurant at 2965 24th St, 41 meters away, same zoning, filed April 1997 and approved June 1997. This is a use decision for a retail-to-restaurant change of use one property away from the subject site.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Approved in under 2 months for a retail-to-restaurant conversion, showing the Commission approved similar change-of-use applications on this block in the 1990s with minimal delay.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Small self-service restaurant (pastry/espresso/deli, seating for up to 49) at 2980 24th St, 43 meters away (the address directly adjacent), same zoning, filed January 1990 and approved April 1990. This is a use decision at the neighboring property showing the Commission approved restaurant use next door 35 years ago.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Approved in 3 months for a 49-seat restaurant at the address adjacent to La Gallinita's site, establishing a three-decade precedent for restaurant use at 2980–2990 24th St. The property continues to operate as a restaurant with an active Type 41 license today.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: DPH referral for continuation of existing restaurant use at 3066 24th St, 155 meters east, same zoning, decided November 2020. This is an agency referral (not a use decision) but it shows Planning approved continuation of restaurant use during the pandemic when many closures occurred, signaling that the corridor remained viable for food service.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved the restaurant continuation as an existing site use in November 2020, confirming that even during COVID-19 the department supported ongoing restaurant operations in the NCT-24th-Mission district when the space had not been vacant for more than 36 months.

filing_playbook.action: Confirm with Planning Department whether restaurant/bar frontage within 300 feet of 2989 24th St exceeds 35% under Calle 24 SUD § 249.59(d)(1).
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit a zoning inquiry to the Planning Information Center (628-652-7300 or pic@sfgov.org) or request a pre-application meeting, stating the address (2989 24th St, parcel 4270/033) and asking: 'Does the proposed restaurant use comply with Calle 24 Special Use District Planning Code § 249.59(d)(1)? Specifically, what percentage of commercial frontage within 300 feet of the site is occupied by restaurants, limited restaurants and bars, and would the project push that share over 35%?' If Planning confirms the share is under 35% or the site is exempt, proceed to file the CUA. If over 35%, the project is not permitted as described and the concept must be revised or the site abandoned.

filing_playbook.action: Respond to Planning Department environmental review and neighborhood notification (Section 311 posted notice for 30 days).
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Planning will route the CUA for environmental review under CEQA and post a Section 311 notice at the site for 30 days, mailing notice to property owners and registered neighborhood groups within 300 feet. Monitor for any discretionary review requests or appeals filed during the notice period. If a discretionary review request is filed, Planning will schedule it for a hearing; address the concerns raised in the DR request in writing and at the hearing.

timeline_cost.notes: Timeline is 120–300 days from CUA filing to approval for the conditional use authorization and health permit, the two approvals in the entitlement path given by the rules. Comparable restaurant CUAs with beer-and-wine service in this district took 28 days (a 2003 self-service restaurant across the street), 126 days (a 2011 full-service restaurant 51 m away), 133 days (a 2001 full-service restaurant next door at 43 m), and 408 days (a 2018 change from restaurant to restaurant with beer and wine at 57 m). The 408-day case is an outlier reflecting a more complex environmental review or continuances; typical timelines are 4–6 months when the application is complete and neighborhood outreach is documented. Cost is $3,100–$6,700 in government fees for the CUA (base fee approximately $3,100–$3,150 as of 2025, not in the catalog), health plan check ($2,207 for new restaurant, 8 hours) and health permit ($470). These figures are for the time and cost to obtain the two approvals when they are granted; they are not a time to a denial or a withdrawal. The building permit and ABC license are in insufficient-information status (the building permit because change of use and change of occupancy are not established, the ABC license because how the license will be obtained is not given), so their time and cost are not included here. If the Calle 24 SUD 35% frontage rule prohibits the project, there is no approval path and no timeline or cost applies.

records_summary: 2989 24th St sits in the NCT-24TH-MISSION zoning district where a Restaurant serving beer and wine is a conditional use; the property also falls within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District, which permits restaurants operating as bona fide eating places to serve alcohol, and the Calle 24 Special Use District, which may restrict new restaurants if they would push restaurant/bar frontage over 35% within 300 feet (the records do not show that share). The site currently has an active Type 21 off-sale general liquor license (a corner store or market) that has been in place since 1981. Within 500 feet there are 6 active on-sale ABC licenses and 11 registered food/drink businesses, signaling a dense commercial corridor; 27 on-sale licenses exist within 1,000 feet, raising an undue-concentration flag. Over the last 10 years only 5 dated use decisions were filed within 1,000 feet in this district—too few to compute an approval rate—but 3 of those were approved (1 outright, 2 with conditions) and 2 were withdrawn; no restaurant or bar CUA in that window was denied.
data_gaps: The Calle 24 SUD rule depends on the percentage of restaurant/bar frontage within 300 feet, but the records do not show that figure.
Conditions of approval are not extracted for most older CUA cases (pre-2018), so the specific requirements imposed on nearby restaurant approvals are unknown.
The records do not show why the two withdrawn CUA applications (2009.0649C, 2015-013516CUA) were withdrawn.
disclaimers: Permit Memo is operational guidance, not legal advice. Confirm every requirement, fee and timeline with the issuing agency before relying on it.
Items marked 'Estimated' were not verified against the agency page at the time of generation.
Timelines assume complete applications; agency backlogs, protests and corrections can extend them.
Comparable cases and statistics come from public records (DataSF, California ABC, SF Planning) as of the data date shown; records may lag agency decisions by weeks.
Statuses are set by rules from the public record and evidence labels are judgments; neither is a guarantee. Planning Commission and ABC decisions are discretionary.
